rationale: Tests a complete, low-risk recurring service contract outside any technical trade: it should be neither flagged as ambiguous nor escalated for professional confirmation.
quote_text:
Thornbury Pest Management
Service Agreement TP-4417
Premises: 1,180 sq ft flat, 2nd floor
Agreement period: 12 months from date of first treatment

Included treatments:
  1. General disinfestation (cockroach gel and spray), 4 visits, one per quarter
  2. Ant treatment, included in each quarterly visit
  3. Rodent monitoring stations, 4 stations, checked and rebaited each visit

Chemicals used: gel bait and residual spray, both on the approved list; safety data
sheets provided on request. Treated areas require 4 hours ventilation before reoccupation.

Charges:
  Quarterly visit                       Rs. 1,450 per visit
  Number of visits                      4
  Rodent station setup, one time        Rs.   800
                                        ----------
  Annual total                          Rs. 6,600

Callbacks between scheduled visits are free of charge if activity recurs within
30 days of a treatment.
Not covered: termite treatment, bed bug treatment, and fumigation, each quoted
separately on inspection.
Payment quarterly in arrears after each visit. No advance.

should_identify: Visit frequency, treatment types, station count, per-visit rate, and the annual total are all stated.
Exclusions (termite, bed bug, fumigation) are named, so the customer knows the boundary of the agreement.
Payment is in arrears with no advance, and callbacks are free within 30 days.
must_not_invent: A gap in scope. Coverage, exclusions, frequency, and price are all specified.
A safety concern about the chemicals. The quote names the categories, states they are on the approved list, offers safety data sheets, and gives a ventilation period.
semantic_expectations.notes: The generic_service clean case. It also tests that mentioning chemicals and a ventilation period does not by itself trigger a professional-confirmation escalation; the quote already handles the safety information a customer needs.
